intent: The floating hint, portalled and positioned beside its trigger with a caret, shown while its Tooltip is open.
typical_uses: A one-line label for its trigger
A label followed by the keyboard shortcut for the same action

dont_use_when.situation: A card-like panel with a heading or several regions

invariants.text: The popup is in the DOM only while the tooltip is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed tooltip renders nothing.

Without `container`, the popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.
Every popup renders a caret, hidden from assistive technology, against the edge that faces the trigger; there is no prop to leave it out.
The popup fades and scales on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` tooltip.module.css drops the scale transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Put paragraphs of text in the popup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep it to a short label - tooltip.module.css caps the popup at 20rem wide, so longer text wraps into a tall block

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; an explicit null renders no popup until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between trigger and popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, instant, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through tooltip.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside TooltipContent; only its `container` is exposed, as TooltipContent's own prop.
Composed inside TooltipContent; its placement props are exposed on TooltipContent itself.
Composed inside TooltipContent as the fixed caret, styled by tooltip.module.css.

good.title: A hint portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: Content with no Tooltip root around it
bad.why: The primitive's Portal and Popup read the nearest Tooltip root's state through context and throw when there is none.
